does: Cooks apples in butter and caramel in a heavy ovenproof pan, covers them with a sheet of pastry and bakes the tart upside down. It is turned out onto a plate, so that the pastry becomes the base and the glossy caramelised apples are on top.
how: Cook the sugar in the pan to a deep amber caramel, take the pan off the heat and stir in the butter.
Pack the halved apples tightly into the caramel, rounded side down, in a ring and then a centre. They shrink as they cook, so they must be crowded.
Cook on the stove until the caramel is thick and the apples have begun to soften and take on colour.
Lay the rolled pastry over the apples and tuck the edge down around them inside the pan. Prick the pastry in a few places.
Bake until the pastry is puffed and deep gold.
Rest the tart for a short while so that the caramel thickens slightly. Lay a plate over the pan and turn both over together with care, because the caramel is very hot.

cues.text: The caramel bubbles up thick and dark around the apples, and the pastry is deep gold and puffed.
A deep smell of caramel and baked apple.

mistakes.mistake: Stopping the caramel when it is pale, so that the tart tastes only sweet.
mistakes.fix: Cook the caramel to a deep amber, taking care that it does not burn.

mistakes.mistake: Packing the apples loosely, so that gaps open as they shrink.
mistakes.fix: Crowd them tightly, because they will shrink.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the tart out at once, when the caramel is runny and still very hot.
mistakes.fix: Rest it briefly so that the caramel thickens, and turn it out over a plate with a deep rim.

comes_after.why: The apples cook in a caramel, so a cook must be able to take sugar to a deep amber without burning it.

variant_of.differs: The fruit goes in the pan first and the pastry on top, and the tart is baked upside down and turned out, so the pastry becomes the base.
